records.overview: Multi-participant healthcare collaboration chat. Consumers invite friends, family, and caregivers into a shared AI-assisted session. All participants have access to all healthcare tools. All conversations constrained to healthcare mission.

features.description: Multiple humans in one conversation with AI assistance
User sends invite link to friends, family, caregivers. No account required.
Multiple AI models participate in the same session (Claude, GPT, etc.), each with access to all tools
All participants (human and AI) can trigger provider search, clinical trials, specialty identification, provider detail
Conversations constrained to healthcare navigation. Same safety filter, emergency detection, scope rules.
Exportable transcript for sharing with doctors, care teams
Each participant manages their own consent tier independently
Session creator (host), invited participant (peer). No admin/enterprise roles.
All participants see messages and AI responses live
Sessions survive disconnects, resumable by invite link

Any participant or component can dispatch a research bot to gather information. Shared object across all three components and pipelines. Bot runs autonomously, returns findings to the session. Dispatched by consensus or individual request. All bot work incurs a fee.

All participants must acknowledge before session continues. Consent re-confirmed.

records.report: FindCare Backend Portability Refactoring — Design Report

problem_statement.summary: The FindCare backend is a 1,323-line monolithic main.py. All business logic, FastAPI setup, prompt construction, tool dispatch, safety checks, provider search, clinical trials, lead capture, notifications, and static file serving live in one file. Porting to a different host (e.g., Azure App Service) requires touching the monolith.
problem_statement.boss_directive: Porting to Azure should not be major work. Portability must be a design property, not an afterthought.
problem_statement.trigger: Delaware Division of Professional Regulation board search URL (https://dpr.delaware.gov/boardsearch/) returns 404 — exposed the need for URL validation AND highlighted how tightly coupled the app is to its hosting environment.

design.principle: Separate what changes per host from what never changes. All business logic is host-agnostic. Only HostConfig and the entry point know where the app is running.

modules.responsibility: Thin entry point. Creates HostConfig from environment, wires URLGuardian, PromptFactory, and FindCareApp together, hands them to GUIHelper, starts the server.
All host-specific configuration in one place. Factory method from_env() reads environment variables with sensible defaults.

modules.constructor: FindCareApp(host_config: HostConfig, prompt_factory: PromptFactory, url_guardian: URLGuardian)
modules.responsibility: ALL business logic. Safety system, provider search, clinical trials, lead capture, chat conversation loop, tool dispatch, notifications, debug logging. Creates its own MongoDB connection and Anthropic/OpenAI clients internally.

Creates the FastAPI app instance. Configures CORS. Registers endpoints (/health, /welcome, /chat). Mounts static files if host_config.mount_static_files is true. Defines Pydantic request/response models.
Loads context documents (PDFs, text files) at init. Constructs the system prompt. Holds the Anthropic tool schema list. Maintains a tool registry (name -> callable) for dispatch.

tool_registry.what: dict[str, Callable] mapping tool names to function references
tool_registry.why: Replaces globals().get(name) — explicit registration, no magic lookup
tool_registry.dispatch: FindCareApp._handle_tool_calls does: fn = self.prompt_factory.get_tool(name); result = fn(**args)

modules.responsibility: Validates URLs in tool results and LLM text responses. Removes broken links, follows redirects, caches results.

methods.check_url(url): Returns (is_valid, redirect_url). HEAD request with GET fallback.
methods.guard_tool_result(result): Validates URLs in a tool result dict. Removes broken links from the 'links' key.
methods.guard_text(text): Validates markdown links and bare URLs in text. Defangs broken links (keeps text, removes href).

features: HEAD request with GET fallback on HTTP 405
Redirect following — updates URL if server redirects
Trusted domain whitelist — Healthgrades, Zocdoc skip validation (bot protection blocks server-side requests)
In-memory TTL cache — avoids repeated HEAD requests within cache window
Concurrent validation — ThreadPoolExecutor for batch URL checks

decisions.gpt_proposed: 11 modules — separate files for DatabaseHelpers, NotificationService, ProviderTools, ClinicalTrialsSearch, ExternalProviderLookup, ContextLoader, ToolDefinitions, etc.
decisions.claude_decided: 5 modules + HostConfig dataclass. Single-function concerns stay as private methods inside FindCareApp.
decisions.rationale: Over-fragmentation adds import complexity for no testability gain. ClinicalTrialsSearch is one function. NotificationService is one function. These don't justify their own files.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: findcare_app.py is ~800 lines — still large. Acceptable because it's cohesive (all business logic) and can be further split in a future sprint if needed.

decisions.topic: Dependency injection for MongoDB and notifications
decisions.gpt_proposed: Inject DatabaseManager and NotificationService into FindCareApp constructor for testability.
decisions.claude_decided: FindCareApp creates its own MongoDB connection and SparkPost notifier internally. NOT injected.
decisions.rationale: human rule: e2e tests use real systems (MongoDB, Anthropic, SparkPost) — no mocks. DI for testability is pointless when you don't mock. Injecting adds constructor complexity for zero practical benefit.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: Harder to unit test FindCareApp in isolation. Mitigated by the fact that this project's testing strategy is e2e with real systems.

decisions.gpt_proposed: _handle_tool_calls lives in PromptFactory alongside tool schemas.
decisions.claude_decided: Tool dispatch stays in FindCareApp. PromptFactory holds only the registry (name -> callable map) and tool schemas.
decisions.rationale: Tool functions (find_providers, record_user_details, etc.) live in FindCareApp and need access to FindCareApp state (DB connection, chat history, IP locks). Dispatch must be in the same class. The registry pattern decouples schema definition from implementation.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: FindCareApp has a dependency on PromptFactory for the registry. Acceptable — they're always used together.

decisions.gpt_proposed: Validate URLs in the final LLM text response only.
decisions.claude_decided: Dual-mode: validate both tool results (guard_tool_result) and LLM text (guard_text).
decisions.rationale: Tool-constructed URLs are the higher-priority fix — we build them deterministically (e.g., Delaware board search). If we know the URL template is broken, we should catch it before the LLM even sees it. Text validation catches anything the LLM generates or hallucinates.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: Two validation points means two places to maintain. Acceptable — both use the same URLGuardian instance and cache.

decisions.claude_decided: Healthgrades and Zocdoc are whitelisted — their search URLs skip validation.
decisions.rationale: Both sites aggressively block server-side requests (bot protection). Our constructed search URLs (e.g., healthgrades.com/search?what=smith) are valid browser URLs but return 403/blocking pages to HEAD/GET from a server. Whitelisting prevents false negatives.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: If Healthgrades or Zocdoc change their URL patterns, broken links would not be caught. Mitigated by the fact that we construct these URLs ourselves with known patterns.

decisions.claude_decided: FindCareApp owns a single Anthropic client instance, created in __init__.
decisions.rationale: Currently the Anthropic client is created fresh in _chat_inner and _safety_check on every call. A single shared instance avoids repeated initialization and is the standard pattern for API clients.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: None — Anthropic SDK client is thread-safe.

decisions.topic: Sprint timing — defer refactoring to Sprint 2
decisions.boss_decided: Do not refactor before the Tuesday 2026-03-31 release. Ship URLGuardian now, refactoring in Sprint 2.
decisions.rationale: App is release-ready. Refactoring 1,323 lines of working code 3 days before deadline is risk with no user-facing payoff. Quality over velocity.
decisions.risk_of_this_decision: main.py stays monolithic through Sprint 1 release. Acceptable — it works, and URLGuardian is the only new capability needed now.

risks.risk: Refactoring may introduce subtle bugs in tool dispatch or chat conversation loop
risks.impact: High — broken chat is a showstopper
risks.mitigation: Each migration step produces a working app. Full e2e test after each step. Stop at any step if tests fail.

risks.risk: URL validation adds latency to chat responses
risks.impact: Medium — user waits longer for responses
risks.mitigation: Concurrent HEAD requests (ThreadPoolExecutor). TTL cache avoids repeated checks. Trusted domain whitelist skips bot-protected sites. Timeout of 5 seconds per URL.

risks.risk: Large PR — 1,300 lines moved across 5 files
risks.impact: Medium — hard to review, merge conflicts with any parallel work
risks.mitigation: Incremental migration steps. Each step is a separate commit. Can stop after any step with a working app.

risks.risk: Trusted domain whitelist becomes stale — Healthgrades/Zocdoc change URL patterns
risks.impact: Low — worst case is a working but outdated search URL
risks.mitigation: We construct these URLs ourselves. If patterns change, update the URL construction in lookup_provider_external.

risks.risk: findcare_app.py at ~800 lines is still large
risks.impact: Low — it's cohesive (all business logic), just long
risks.mitigation: Can further split in a future sprint if needed. Provider tools and safety system are natural extraction candidates.

records.executive_summary: Modular monolith refactor of FindCare backend from a 1,712-line main.py monolith to a facade-oriented domain architecture. Two business domains (FindCare, EvaluateCareQuality) with explicit service classes per UAT feature. HuggingFace reduced to entrypoint + adapter only. Strangler Fig migration in 7 phases, zero downtime, deployable at every phase. Pydantic-enforced tool boundaries. Full Perplexity audit response covering all 18 findings.

consent_flow.title: Consent Framework — Full Workflow Design
consent_flow.description: HIPAA-aligned two-tier consent framework controlling what user data is stored and how. Consent is a full-time workflow — not a flag. It governs the entire data lifecycle of a user session.
consent_flow.trigger: Every 5th user message, system prompt instructs Claude to ask: 'Would you like someone from ChatHealthy.AI to follow up with you personally?'

tiers.name: Verbatim Consent
tiers.prompt: May we save a verbatim transcript of this conversation with your contact details?

if_yes.stored: Full chat_history (PII intact), email, name, notes, reason_for_contact
if_yes.evidence: Consent exchange itself is included in the stored transcript

tiers.name: De-Identified Summary Consent
tiers.prompt: May we save a de-identified summary of this conversation instead?

if_yes.stored: LLM-generated summary passed through deIdentify() — no PII, no chat_history
if_yes.process: Claude summarizes -> deIdentify() scrubs PII -> stored in notes field

if_no.stored: Contact fields only (email, name). No history, no summary.

data_streams.treatment: Always de-identified before storage. No PII. No consent needed.
Two-tier consent governs what is stored. User chooses verbatim or summary.

integration_points: ChatOrchestrator: triggers consent prompt every 5th message
LeadService: delegates to ConsentService for data handling
System Prompt: RULE 7 defines the consent UX flow
deIdentify(): shared utility used by ConsentService and UnknownQuestionService
regulatory_notes: Consent exchange itself must be preserved as evidence (included in verbatim transcript)
De-identification must be applied BEFORE storage, not after
Emergency records (BTC-003) must NEVER be deleted regardless of consent state
Test data tagged with testdata=true for filtering

growth_trajectory.note: This service will GROW, not diminish. Consent is a first-class, expanding concern.
planned_additions: Granular consent: per-data-type consent (contact info separate from conversation history)
Consent revocation: user can withdraw consent after the fact — must retroactively de-identify or delete
Consent audit trail: immutable log of every consent grant, revocation, and data action
HIPAA minimum necessary: only collect what is needed for the stated purpose
Consent expiration: time-limited consent with re-confirmation workflow
Enterprise consent: when healthcare orgs use the platform, their compliance policies override defaults
Consent portability: export consent records for regulatory audit (state AG, HHS OCR)
Multi-jurisdiction: state-specific consent rules (e.g., California CCPA, NY SHIELD, HIPAA federal)
growth_trajectory.architectural_implication: ConsentService must be its own bounded context with dedicated tools, dedicated pydantic models, dedicated tests, and dedicated audit logging. It is NOT a helper inside LeadService.

architectural_decisions.decision: Facade-oriented domains over flat service layer
architectural_decisions.rationale: Two business domains (FindCare, EvaluateCareQuality) each get a facade. Facades are the ONLY entry point from ToolRouter to domain services. Prevents cross-domain coupling.
Claude sends JSON tool arguments. Pydantic validates at the ToolRouter before reaching domain services. Catches schema mismatches early.

architectural_decisions.rationale: Per human decision. Prompt references tool names only (not class names). ToolRouter is source of truth for available tools.

architectural_decisions.decision: Provider Detail belongs to EvaluateCareQuality (not FindCare)
architectural_decisions.rationale: Provider detail is a quality evaluation concern (NPI lookup, board certifications, ratings). Finding a provider and evaluating their quality are distinct business actions.

architectural_decisions.decision: Frontend remains thin — no domain duplication
architectural_decisions.rationale: All domain logic stays server-side. Frontend is presentation-only: ChatWindow, MessageBubble, EmergencyBanner. No backend domain structure mirrored.
7 phases, each deployable. Old functions remain callable until replaced. Zero downtime throughout migration.

records.title: Pipeline Architecture v2 -- Consensus Design (Claude + GPT-4.1)
records.overview: Comprehensive pipeline architecture for healthcare data processing. Addresses NPPES provider data (10.6GB), CMS Part D prescriber data (3.7GB), OIG/SAM exclusion lists, and molecule-to-indication crosswalk. Designed for Azure Functions (Durable), MongoDB Atlas, Azure Blob Storage.
priority_goals: 1. RELIABILITY -- pipeline must complete or resume from last checkpoint. No data loss. Parity verification mandatory.
2. SPEED -- parallel where possible. Fan-out per state. Download in parallel. Process in parallel.
3. COST -- minimize compute time on Azure Functions. Minimize MongoDB Atlas cluster uptime. Pause when not running.

1_pipeline_topology.provider_pipeline: NPPES download -> partition -> load -> county enrichment (6 passes) -> embed -> ship
1_pipeline_topology.prescriber_evaluate_care_pipeline: CMS Part D download -> load -> crosswalk enrichment -> OIG/SAM flags -> specialty normalization -> embed

2_orchestration.sub_orchestrators: Each pipeline stage is a sub-orchestrator with fan-out/fan-in
2_orchestration.deterministic_replay: All I/O in activity functions only. Orchestrators are pure state machines.
2_orchestration.checkpoint: Automatic checkpoint at every yield (Durable Functions built-in)
2_orchestration.start_step: Resume from any stage via start_step parameter
2_orchestration.v4_001: Pipeline runs on Azure Functions, not local machines

3_download_layer.streaming: Stream to Azure Blob Storage (ADLS Gen2), never full file in memory
3_download_layer.parallel_downloads: NPPES, CMS Part D, OIG, SAM, RxNorm fetched concurrently via task_all
3_download_layer.resumable: Range reads with checkpoint-aware logic; resume from last successful byte on failure
3_download_layer.snapshot_manifest: Pipeline-level manifest tracks all input files with ETag/SHA/version for consistency

provider_load.method: Byte-aligned CSV partitioning -> N workers fan-out via task_all
provider_load.partitioning: Newline-aligned boundaries computed from blob byte ranges
provider_load.idempotent: Upsert by NPI, safe to re-run

prescriber_load.method: Streaming CSV reader with chunked reads
prescriber_load.memory_safety: Never load full file in memory. O(1) per-row memory. Hard process-level RAM quotas.
prescriber_load.pre_ingest_dry_run: Scan first N rows to estimate row width, cardinality, memory footprint. Refuse ingest or force chunking if risk detected.
prescriber_load.chunking: Adaptive chunk size (default 100MB or 100k rows, whichever first). Dynamic adjustment based on observed RAM usage.

4_processing_layer.worker_pattern: PipelineWorkerBase template method (Gang of Four) for all batch workers
4_processing_layer.chunk_state_machine: Each chunk has explicit state: pending -> in_progress -> complete -> verified | failed

parked_items.topic: External Vector DB vs MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
parked_items.claude_position: Keep MongoDB Atlas Vector Search for now. Current 1.3M providers with 3072d vectors is within Atlas M30 capacity if indexes are only on frontend cluster. The 199% RAM issue is because vector indexes were on the pipeline cluster (which is undersized). Moving to external DB adds operational complexity and cost for marginal benefit at current scale.
parked_items.gpt_position: Mandate external vector DB immediately. MongoDB Atlas Vector Search is not designed for massive, high-dimensional, write-heavy workloads. RAM pressure will only grow as states are added. Move to Pinecone, Qdrant, or Azure Cognitive Search now.
parked_items.resolution: PARKED. Monitor RAM on frontend cluster after pipeline cluster vector indexes are removed. If frontend cluster RAM exceeds 80%, evaluate external vector DB. Re-evaluate at 2M providers.

parked_items.topic: Parquet as Canonical Intermediate Format vs Direct CSV-to-MongoDB
parked_items.claude_position: Adding Parquet as an intermediate format adds significant complexity (new dependencies, format conversion, Parquet writer/reader infrastructure) for a pipeline that currently processes 4 states. The CSV-to-MongoDB path works and is well-understood. Parquet makes sense at 10x scale.
parked_items.gpt_position: Parquet should be the canonical format from day one. It is natively splittable, schema-aware, columnar, and cloud-native. CSV is fragile (encoding, quoting, field splitting). Investment now prevents costly migration later.
parked_items.resolution: PARKED. Current pipeline continues with CSV-to-MongoDB. Add Parquet conversion as a future sprint item when scaling to all 50 states. Schema registry concept is adopted for metadata tracking regardless.

parked_items.topic: Distributed Commit Log (CosmosDB) vs MongoDB-based Checkpointing
parked_items.claude_position: MongoDB admin collections are sufficient for checkpoint state. Adding CosmosDB as a commit log introduces a new service dependency, new cost, and new failure mode. The pipeline already uses Durable Functions for orchestration state.
parked_items.gpt_position: MongoDB is not designed for high-throughput, low-latency commit log workloads. CosmosDB or an append-only ADLS log provides stronger consistency guarantees and avoids circular dependency (checkpointing in the same DB being written to).
parked_items.resolution: PARKED. Keep MongoDB checkpointing for now. If checkpoint writes become a bottleneck or cause contention with data writes, evaluate ADLS append-only log as alternative. Durable Functions replay is the primary checkpoint mechanism.

parked_items.claude_position: A full schema registry service is over-engineering for 4 data sources (NPPES, CMS Part D, OIG, SAM) that change schemas at most annually. Schema validation in code (field count check, header match) is sufficient.
parked_items.gpt_position: A schema registry is essential for contract enforcement, drift detection, and automated compatibility testing. Even with few sources, schema drift is a real risk and causes silent data corruption.
parked_items.resolution: COMPROMISE. Implement lightweight schema validation in code (header match + field count + type checks). Store schema fingerprints (SHA-256) per batch in admin.DataLoadMetadata. Defer full registry service to all-50-states scale.

parked_items.claude_position: The architecture should be as simple as possible for current scale (1.3M providers, 4 states). Many GPT recommendations (multi-region active-active, ADLS Gen2 landing zones, distributed commit logs, schema registries) are appropriate for enterprise scale but premature for a startup processing 4 states.
parked_items.gpt_position: Building for scale from day one prevents costly rewrites. Healthcare data grows rapidly. The cost of retrofitting fault tolerance is higher than building it in.
parked_items.resolution: COMPROMISE. Adopt the core reliability patterns (chunked streaming, checkpoint/restart, parity verification, circuit breakers) now. Defer enterprise-scale infrastructure (multi-region, external vector DB, schema registry service, distributed commit log) to the all-50-states milestone.

schema_evolution_detail.strategy: Schema evolution is handled via Parquet's built-in support for optional columns. Each Parquet file stores the exact schema used for that batch in file metadata.
process: 1. On ingest, detect schema changes by comparing normalized schema fingerprint to previous batches.
2. If new columns are added, Parquet files include them as nullable fields.
3. If columns are dropped, they are omitted from new files; readers must handle missing fields as null.
4. All schema changes are logged in admin.SchemaFingerprints and referenced in the conversion manifest.
5. Downstream readers must use schema merging when reading multiple files across schema versions.
schema_evolution_detail.backward_compatibility: Always prefer additive (new nullable columns) or reorder-tolerant changes. Breaking changes (type changes, column drops) require operator approval and are blocked by default.

reconciliation_query.description: Find all chunks that have a 'chunk_complete' event in the commit log but no corresponding checkpoint document in MongoDB.
steps: 1. Use Synapse or Spark to extract all chunk_id and pipeline_run_id from commit log entries where event_type = 'chunk_complete'.
2. Query admin.DataLoadMetadata for documents with matching pipeline_run_id and chunk_id, state='complete'.
3. Return all (pipeline_run_id, chunk_id) pairs present in the commit log but missing in MongoDB.
reconciliation_query.pseudo_sql: SELECT c.pipeline_run_id, c.chunk_id FROM commit_log c WHERE c.event_type = 'chunk_complete' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM admin.DataLoadMetadata m WHERE m.pipeline_run_id = c.pipeline_run_id AND m.chunk_id = c.chunk_id AND m.state = 'complete')

write_order: 1. Write commit log entry to ADLS append blob (commit_logs/...).
2. On successful commit log write, update MongoDB checkpoint (admin.DataLoadMetadata) with commit_log_ref.

3. If MongoDB update fails after commit log write, retry up to 3 times with exponential backoff. If still failing, alert ops and mark chunk as 'checkpoint_pending' in a special admin.CheckpointPending collection.

commit_log_write_fails_first.action: Do NOT update MongoDB checkpoint. Worker retries commit log write up to 3 times (with backoff). If still failing, chunk remains in 'in_progress' state and is picked up for retry by the reconciliation job.

commit_log_write_succeeds_but_mongo_chec.action: Retry MongoDB checkpoint up to 3 times. If still failing, log to admin.CheckpointPending and alert ops. The reconciliation job will attempt to re-apply the checkpoint using the commit log as the source of truth.

reconciliation_job_detail.description: A scheduled job (Azure Function TimerTrigger) runs every 15 minutes to compare commit log and checkpoint state.
steps: 1. Enumerate all 'chunk_complete' events in commit log for the last 24 hours.
2. For each, check for a corresponding 'complete' checkpoint in admin.DataLoadMetadata.
3. If commit log entry exists but no checkpoint, attempt to re-apply the checkpoint using the commit log details.
4. If checkpoint exists but no commit log entry, flag as 'commit_log_missing' in admin.CheckpointPending and alert ops.
5. All reconciliation actions are logged to admin.ReconciliationLog.

commit_log_missing.description: Checkpoint exists but no commit log entry.
action: 1. Attempt to reconstruct the missing commit log entry from checkpoint and pipeline context.
2. Write reconstructed entry to commit log with a 'recovered' flag.
3. Alert ops for manual review if reconstruction is ambiguous.

checkpoint_missing.description: Commit log entry exists but no MongoDB checkpoint.
action: 1. Attempt to re-apply the checkpoint to MongoDB using commit log details.
2. If re-apply fails, alert ops and mark chunk as 'checkpoint_recovery_failed' in admin.CheckpointPending.

pipeline_run_failure: 1. Alert: Immediate email and dashboard alert to ops@chathealthy.ai and on-call engineer (PagerDuty integration) on any pipeline abort or unhandled exception.
2. Diagnosis: Operator reviews failure logs in admin.DataLoadMetadata and commit log for error context.
3. Checkpoint Review: Identify last successful chunk/stage from checkpoints.
4. Data Consistency: Run reconciliation query to ensure no partial chunks are marked complete.
5. Remediation: Address root cause (e.g., fix code, resolve quota, restart failed service).
6. Resume: Restart pipeline using start_step parameter at last successful stage/chunk.
7. Postmortem: Log incident in admin.IncidentLog and update runbook if new failure mode discovered.
parquet_file_corruption: 1. Alert: Immediate alert to ops@chathealthy.ai and dashboard if Parquet validation fails during load.
2. Quarantine: Move corrupted Parquet file to /corrupted/ partition in ADLS Gen2.
3. Diagnosis: Operator inspects file integrity (e.g., pyarrow validation, CRC check, schema mismatch).
4. Recovery: If possible, re-convert original CSV to Parquet and replace corrupted file.
5. Resume: Re-run Parquet-to-MongoDB load for affected partition.
6. Escalation: If original source is unavailable, escalate to data provider and document in admin.IncidentLog.
commit_log_checkpoint_disagreement: 1. Alert: Immediate alert to ops@chathealthy.ai and dashboard if reconciliation job detects mismatch.
2. Diagnosis: Operator reviews admin.CheckpointPending and commit log entries for affected chunk(s).
3. Recovery Path A (commit log exists, checkpoint missing): Re-apply checkpoint using commit log details.
4. Recovery Path B (checkpoint exists, commit log missing): Attempt to reconstruct and append missing commit log entry; flag as 'recovered'.
5. Manual Review: If automated recovery fails, escalate for manual operator intervention.
6. Documentation: Log all actions in admin.ReconciliationLog and update runbook if new scenario is found.

resolved_parked_items.decision: Stay with MongoDB Atlas Vector Search (frontend cluster only). No external vector DB.
resolved_parked_items.rationale: human: Already invested in Atlas, external DB adds ops burden. RAM monitored; offload only if >80% or 2M providers.

resolved_parked_items.topic: Parquet as Canonical Intermediate Format vs Direct CSV-to-MongoDB
resolved_parked_items.decision: Parquet is canonical intermediate format. All ingest and downstream processing use Parquet.
resolved_parked_items.rationale: human: CSV fragility will bite us at 50-state scale. Better to invest now.

resolved_parked_items.topic: Distributed Commit Log vs MongoDB-based Checkpointing
resolved_parked_items.decision: Implement both: ADLS append-only commit log (audit trail) and MongoDB checkpoint (operational state).
resolved_parked_items.rationale: human: Different purposes. Commit log = what happened; checkpoint = where are we now.

resolved_parked_items.decision: Lightweight schema validation in code (header match, field count, type check) + schema fingerprint per batch.
resolved_parked_items.rationale: human: Full registry not needed for 4 sources. Fingerprints and validation suffice.

resolved_parked_items.decision: Full reliability patterns NOW: chunked streaming, checkpoint/restart, parity verification, circuit breakers, dead letters.
resolved_parked_items.rationale: human: 'If not now, when.' No more deferral.

Parity verification (count + hash spot checks) before declaring Ship success
Worker lease/heartbeat pattern for claiming records in enrichment and embedding
Circuit breaker pattern for external API enrichment
Exponential backoff with jitter for all external API calls
Dead-letter queues for irrecoverable enrichment failures
ClusterLifecycleManager for pipeline cluster pause/resume
Durable Functions replay as primary checkpoint mechanism
Per-worker metadata in admin.DataLoadMetadata
OpenTelemetry integration for distributed tracing
